description_full: On Holding AG, together with its subsidiaries, develops and distributes performance sports products under the On brand in Switzerland, the rest of Europe, the Middle East, Africa, the United States, the rest of the Americas, and the Asia-Pacific. The company offers athletic footwear, apparel, and accessories for performance running, performance outdoor, performance all day, performance training, performance tennis, and young movers. It sells its products to athletes and active customers through wholesale and direct-to-consumer channels; run specialty, general sporting goods, outdoor, luxury, street fashion, and lifestyle retailers; owned retail stores; and e-commerce platforms. On Holding AG was founded in 2010 and is headquartered in Zurich, Switzerland.
ceo_bio: Mr. David  Allemann | Co-Founder, Co-CEO & Executive Co-Chairman | Age 54
culture_narrative: Employs approximately 3K people. Revenue per employee of $907K ranks in the top quartile among Consumer Cyclical peers, with revenue growing 46%/yr across its filed history. Each employee generates $86K of free cash flow annually.
financial_summary: On Holding AG is a large-cap consumer cyclical business with a $11.3B market cap on $3.6B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +42% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +8.0pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 33% against a 11% cost of capital — a 22-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat. Gross margins of 60% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $342M in free cash flow — roughly 10 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.76× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 13× is fortress-like.

Net dilution runs at 0.0% annually, transferring value from owners to stock-based comp, and insiders hold 24% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 1.6× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

sect: Its 13% operating margin runs 5pp above the Consumer Cyclical median (7%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It captures 1.58x its revenue share in sector profits, taking a disproportionate slice of the profit pool.
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 377 companies in the universe; the top four hold 26% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares have drifted lower, down 16% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 34% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 50% and a beta of 1.39, it amplifies market moves.
Liquidity is deep, with about $299.9M traded a day, and interest is running hot at 1.6x its yearly average volume.
In past sell-offs it fell 59% in the 2022 bear market.
val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $31.11 (margin of safety -8%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 54%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $24.24 to $41.04 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks expensive against Consumer Cyclical peers: EV/EBITDA 34.6 vs 10.7 and P/FCF 32.9 vs 16.7 (sector median).
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 3.0% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 2.2% (vs the 8% bar).
The 31 covering analysts target $43.60 on average, 30% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
The price implies 13.7% annual cash-flow growth, 2pp more than the model expects.
prof: ROIC of 33% clears the cost of capital of 11.3% by 22pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 3.85).
It runs a 60% gross margin and converts 10% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 1.76x.
ROE of 12% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.7x equity multiplier).
Operating margin is running 9pp above its own historical average, a peak-margin risk if conditions normalise.
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $1.3B.
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 6.9, in the safe zone).
growth: Revenue has compounded at 41.6% over 3 years, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 12%).
At current returns, reinvesting 59% of profits supports about 19.6% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
It has beaten earnings estimates by 33.9% on average.
Analysts expect 14.3% long-term annual earnings growth.
own: Insiders own 24.2%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 69%.
Insider trading is two-way: 2 purchases and 2 sales over the past year, net $3.9M bought.
Short interest is elevated at 11.6% of the float, 2.9 days to cover.
people: With about 3,963 employees, each generates about $907K of revenue, 2.4x the Consumer Cyclical median, and revenue has grown 46.3% a year across its filed history.
That works out to $86K of free cash flow per employee.
The company is founder-led, which often keeps management aligned with long-term owners.
